guides.name: Robert Walters Middle East Salary Survey 2026 (26th edition) - Saudi Arabia tables
guides.dataAsOf: Placements made during 2025 plus predictions for 2026; methodology: over 100,000 roles advertised in the Middle East over a 12-month period (p. 5)
guides.basis: Permanent salary per month, range + average; 'basic salaries and rates, exclusive of benefits/bonuses unless otherwise specified' (p. 5). Saudi Arabia table headers print the currency as AED (verified on rendered pp. 24, 33, 49); recorded as printed.
guides.method: Direct PDF download (no form). Saudi Arabia pages 16-17, 23-25, 31-33, 39-40, 45, 49, 53, 57, 61 parsed from the PyMuPDF text layer (single-column tables); text layer checked against rendered page images of pp. 24, 33, 49 and matched row for row.

guides.name: Michael Page Saudi Arabia Salary Guide 2027 (online salary guide)
guides.dataAsOf: 'Assignments completed for clients between 1 January and 30 Septemeber [sic] 2026' plus consultant conversations, database and sector research (guide FAQ)
guides.basis: 'Salaries are shown in thousands of Saudi Riyal (SAR) and reflect the average monthly salary in KSA, including basic, hosuing, transporation and other allowances, excluding bonuses and commissions' (guide FAQ, typos as printed). Role pages show Low / Medium / High.
guides.method: Latest edition online is 2027 (the 2026 KSA edition is no longer served). Sector tables and 'Download' buttons are gated behind a details form (not submitted). Each role's public page (/salary-guide-sa/sa/<sector>/<role>) prints Low/Medium/High in its HTML without any form; values read from the served HTML with curl ('SAR 40.000' = 40,000). Default view = no experience/company-size filter. Role pages are headed 'Yearly salary for ...' although the FAQ says monthly; recorded as monthly.

guides.name: Hays Saudi Arabia Salary Guide 2026
guides.basis: Total fixed monthly salary package, SAR
guides.method: Re-checked only for the families with no salary (local copy; text dump plus rendered pp. 34 Construction & property and 38 Marketing). No row for planning/scheduling, MEP, hospitality/front office, events, video/motion, translation, medical coding/RCM, UX research or gaming, so no Hays rows added.
